findings.claim: The guard at line 1179 is inverted: `if (stringMembers.ContainsKey(member.StringKey)) stringMembers.Add(...)`. The dictionary starts empty, so a string-keyed member in this second member loop is never added. Every such member is silently left out of the generated map-mode formatter, so its data is neither written nor read. If the key were somehow already present, `Add` would throw instead. Builds with `SuppressSourceGeneration` unset are affected, which breaks the 'unchanged behaviour' criterion.

It compiles a [MessagePackObject] with a public field [Key("f")] FieldValue and a property [Key("p")] PropValue, then asserts the generated source references both. On head one of them is missing.

findings.claim: Duplicate keys (two members with [Key(0)] or the same string key) used to throw from Dictionary.Add. They are now silently de-duplicated: the second member is dropped from the generated formatter and no diagnostic is reported. The user gets a formatter that silently skips a member, whereas the dynamic resolver rejects duplicate keys.
